about: Two runs of the Jülich bottleneck experiment played at once as two phone cameras: the main gate (run 030, played twice) and side door B (run 160). The venue layout is a SAMPLE; the measurements, Muse Spark's decisions, Glimmer's checks, the counts, the acks and the evidence chain are what the live system recorded.

report.instruction: यह कैमरा मुख्य गेट को ऊपर से देखता है। गेट के सामने भीड़ खतरनाक होने से पहले हमें चेतावनी दें। हमारी योजना: मुख्य गेट भरने लगे तो प्रवेश गलियारे की भीड़ को साइड डोर B की ओर मोड़ें। स्टीवर्ड्स को बताएं क्या करना है और हिंदी और अंग्रेज़ी में शांति से घोषणा करें।

timeline.text: gate approach (2 x 2 m): peak 8.249 people/m² (33 people)

Gate approach is 8.2 ppm2 with 33 people in 4 sqm and pressure 0.094, well into crush range. Side door B at 3.75 ppm2 and filling at +2.75 per min cannot take redirected flow, so inflow must be held instead.

Sent (Glimmer confirmed: The overhead view shows a very dense cluster of people wearing orange hats tightly packed in front of the gate turnstiles. The crowd occupies the gate approach zone and is essentially stationary / very slow moving. Individuals are shoulder-to-shoulder with little visible free space between bodies; the group forms a compact mass with heads almost touching. Motion arrows inside the yellow gate approach box are short and mostly upward/ inward, indicating minimal forward progress and essentially no outflow through the gate. Staff in blue vests are present at the gate and to the side of the cluster. The surrounding entry corridor is much less occupied. No clear falling bodies are individually discernible at this resolution, but the packing density is extreme and movement is effectively arrested, consistent with a crush-range condition at the Main gate approach. Side door B is not visible in this camera view.)

after_action.headline: Crush-range crowding at the Main gate approach peaked at 8.249 people/m² and cleared by 01:37:58Z after a confirmed-critical alert, bilingual hold announcements, and steward/safety-officer response.
after_action.narrative: From clip start 01:35:21.143524Z phone-10 overhead of the Main gate, the gate approach (2 x 2 m) peaked at 8.249 people/m² (33 people) at 01:35:28.213597Z, while entry corridor peaked at 1.972 people/m² (74 people) and view at 0.971 people/m² (77 people) at 01:35:22.143524Z. Gate approach averaged 5.249 people/m² with 108.9 s above 2, 96.9 s above 4, 72.8 s above 5 and 60.8 s above 6, max pressure 0.1373, then eased to 0.5 people/m² (2 people, pressure 0.0031) by 01:37:58.561323Z after still being 8.25 people/m² at 01:37:04.200507Z and 3.5 people/m² at 01:37:38.115512Z. For critical alert crowd-9960776a5934 the peak reading at 01:35:28.213597Z was assessed in 25.8 s and sent confirmed-critical in 41.1 s at 01:36:09.284623Z, with stewards notified at 01:36:03.652930Z, safety_officer escalated at 01:36:49.093160Z, safety_officer ack 'On my way' at 01:36:52.035936Z, and 2 x blue-vest arrival at 01:36:57.993649Z. At 01:36:09.284623Z calm Hindi and English announcements asked crowds to stay in place, not push, and follow stewards — '[hi] Kripya dhyaan dein...' and '[en] Please wait where you are...' (heard back same meaning) — while stewards were told to hold inflow at Outer queue barrier, hold Entry corridor, and send stewards to Main gate; the planned redirect of entry-corridor flow to Side door B was not used because it was assessed as too full to take flow. Ground truth (Jülich bottleneck run 030_c_56_h0, 11 readings) shows counts were close (gate approach count_ratio 0.996 MAE 1.0, entry corridor 0.997 MAE 1.0) but density was low: gate-approach true peak 9.52 vs system 8.249 and entry-corridor true peak 2.47 vs system 1.972 (median density ratios 1.0 and 0.78); unknowns remain that densities rest on owner (±0.00 m) floor calibration with extrapolation past calibrated floor, and SAM 3.1 misses people hidden behind others.

check.seen: The crowd is stacked up against the Side door B / side door approach area. The yellow outlined side door approach (2x2 m) is densely filled with people in orange hats standing shoulder-to-shoulder in the queue funnel formed by the barriers. The people are packed tightly in the approach zone and the adjacent side queue, with the densest clustering immediately in front of the door structure on the right side of the image. Motion is very limited; the group is essentially static and compressed against the barriers and the door threshold. No people are visible moving out through the door and the door/doorway structure itself remains closed / unoccupied on the egress side. No clear pushing, swaying, falls or a visibly blocked exit beyond the normal queue compression is discernible in the two frames provided, but the packing is high and the crowd is essentially at a standstill with little free space for movement in the approach zone. The annotated overlay on the newest frame shows side door approach (2x2 m): 9 people, 2.2/m2 and side queue: 56, 1.5/m2, with a 3.0/m2 peak cell in the approach, consistent with stacking at Side door B with no outflow visible.

tallies.glimmer_note: The un-greyed photographic area shows a dense overhead crowd wearing orange/red hats. Roughly three dozen orange-hatted heads are visible in the non-grey portion of the frame, with a number of heads only partly visible / overlapped by neighbours. The exact number is hard to pin down because of overlap and the tilted crop, but the visible orange heads in the un-greyed region are on the order of ~32-35, about 33 can be reliably distinguished.

The un-greyed / image area is a top-down view of a small group. Six heads are unambiguously in the image area – five of them wearing the bright orange hats that dominate the view and one further head/upper-torso that is partly visible at the top-right of the frame. A seventh head/upper-torso is only very partially clipped at the extreme right edge of the un-greyed area, so the clearly countable heads in the non-greyed region are six, with a seventh very partial one at the edge.

The un-greyed, tilted crop shows a dense crowd seen from above, most wearing bright orange hats/caps. Counting the orange heads that fall inside the non-grey image area, including those that are partially occluded by neighbours, gives roughly three dozen heads. A careful manual tally of the visible orange caps in the crop is about 31 heads.

The un-greyed / image area shows a top-down view of a small group. Seven heads are discernible in the visible portion of the frame: five with bright orange hats/beanies and two additional heads – one in a white/light cap between the two upper orange hats and one partially visible at the top-right edge of the image – all of which lie within the non-greyed image area. People that are only partly hidden by others are included in this tally.
